claim: The host's 2026-07-18 patch fixed a weakly-connected-component exploit in the division metric: pre-patch a GT division counted as TP if the matched predicted nodes merely shared ONE connected component containing ANY predicted fork, so a large connected blob with forks scored TPs everywhere. The patch replaces that with directed local topology.
quote: commit aa65e90aeb8a774ebb1b549e547787b87ac8a01c  Author: Thibaut Goldsborough  Date: Fri Jul 17 16:47:48 2026 -0700   updating metric to patch weakly connected component exploit

claim: The patched metric.md states the directed-topology requirement explicitly: sharing a weakly connected component is no longer sufficient; the parent anchor must be the predicted fork or its immediate predecessor and daughter matches must lie downstream of the fork on their assigned branches.
quote: Directed local topology. The parent anchor must be the predicted fork or its immediate predecessor, and the daughter matches must lie downstream of the fork on their assigned branches. Merely sharing a weakly connected component is not sufficient.

claim: The same patch silently widened what counts as a predicted fork from 'exactly two' to 'at least two' outgoing edges, so any over-linked node with out-degree >= 2 is now evaluated as a division claim and can become a division false positive.
quote: A ground-truth cell division has exactly two outgoing edges. During evaluation, any predicted node with at least two outgoing edges is treated as a predicted fork.

claim: LIVE EXPLOIT #1 (division term): a predicted fork is only a false positive when there is local GT evidence - the fork must itself match (within 7 um) a GT node with out-degree >= 1, or its child/grandchild branches must match nodes in two different GT components. Ground truth is ~2.8% annotated, so roughly 35 of every 36 forks a solution emits are literally invisible to the division metric: no TP, no FP. A fork proposer therefore only needs ~3% GLOBAL precision to break even.

The same asymmetry holds on the edge term: a predicted edge is only an FP if one of its endpoints matches a GT node that GT connects to a different partner; all other predicted edges are ignored. So a spurious fork on an unannotated nucleus costs nothing in EITHER term, and the entire cost of an aggressive division proposer is confined to the ~2.8% of nuclei that are annotated.
source: royerlab metrics.md (Edge Jaccard section) + competition Evaluation page
quote: All other predicted edges are ignored by our metric. ... Because the ground truth is sparse, a correct prediction will inevitably include nodes and edges the ground truth doesn't cover. Predicted nodes that do not match a ground-truth node are not counted as false positives.

claim: LIVE EXPLOIT #2 (edge term): the node-count adjustment has no upper clamp, only a lower one. adjusted_jaccard = max(0, jaccard * (1 - 0.1*(T_pred - T_true)/T_true)). Under-predicting nodes multiplies the score by MORE than 1.0 - up to 1.1x as T_pred approaches zero. The host acknowledges this on the Evaluation page.
quote: adjusted_jaccard = max(0, jaccard · (1 − a · (T_pred − T_true) / T_true))  ...  Due to the nature of the metric, it is possible for scores to exceed 1.0.

claim: T_true is not hidden - it is read from the GEFF metadata key 'estimated_number_of_nodes', which ships with the input data, so a submission can read its own target node count at inference time and tune T_pred to sit at or just under it for a free multiplier >= 1.0.
quote:
n_total
        Target node count (e.g. from the GEFF ``estimated_number_of_nodes``
        metadata extra).

claim: At least one strong competitor (hengck23) has independently spotted the node-count lever and plans a density head specifically to hit the estimated node count, calling it a metric hack - so this edge-term exploit is not undiscovered, only under-exploited.
quote: (4) maybe a head to predict node density so that i can predict kaggle estimate node count (metric hack)

claim: The same patch added three undocumented submission-shaping rules to the edge metric: edges whose endpoints are not exactly one timepoint apart are silently DROPPED (so gap-closing t+2 links contribute nothing), duplicate edges mapping onto the same GT edge are collapsed to the lowest edge id, and out-degree is capped at 2 by keeping the TWO LOWEST EDGE IDs per source - so CSV row order decides which two arcs of an over-linked node survive.
quote: Cap out-degree: a dividing cell has at most two children, so a predicted node with more than two outgoing edges is biologically invalid. Keep the two edges with the lowest EDGE_ID per source and drop the rest with a warning.

claim: The merge-collapse rule in the same commit killed a second, edge-term exploit that hengck23 had published two days earlier: duplicating tracks with new ids to inflate edge TPs, because the metric did not penalise fragmentation or duplication.
quote: i find a metric hack: you make a graph. if your just repeat your tracks (giving new id) your edge_jaccard is not affected. this is the cause the kaggle metric don't penalize fragmentation, duplication. hence you can create multiple almost smiliar tracks to improve TP.

claim: The synthetic generator reproduces the evaluator's exact XY downsample (a stride vol[:, ::4, ::4], not a block mean) and reports DoG detectability of 0.89/0.76 on synthetic vs 0.91-0.94 on real annotated nuclei - i.e. it is calibrated to be slightly HARDER than the real data, not easier.

claim: MEASURED DIVISION GEOMETRY (n=7 labelled divisions, 4 films): a division step is 2-4x a normal continuation step and daughters appear already far apart - median longest parent-daughter step 8.47 um (range 5.69-13.65), median sister separation at prediction 10.22 um (7.87-13.12), against a ~3 um labelled continuation step.

longest parent to daughter step   median 8.47 um   range 5.69 to 13.65

claim: THE SINGLE BIGGEST ACTIONABLE NUMBER: the metric's own 7 um matching radius, reused as a linking gate, admits BOTH daughter arcs in only 2 of 7 divisions (29%); a 9.9 um gate gets 5/7, 12 um gets 6/7 and 15 um gets 7/7. A gate tuned for continuations rejects the second arc before out-degree capacity is ever consulted, so allowing out-degree 2 is necessary but NOT sufficient.
quote:
both steps inside a  7.0 um gate    2/7   (29%)
both steps inside a  9.9 um gate    5/7   (71%)
both steps inside a 12.0 um gate    6/7   (86%)
both steps inside a 15.0 um gate    7/7  (100%)

claim: Detection is NOT the ceiling on divisions: on 7 labelled divisions the parent and BOTH daughters were detected 7/7 within the metric's own 7 um radius, yet zero of 14 parent-daughter edges were produced and predicted parent out-degree was 1 every single time. Upper bound 100%, achieved 0%.
quote:
parent and both daughters detected       7/7   (100%)
both parent->daughter edges in my graph  0/7
exactly one edge present                 7/7
predicted parent out-degree              1, every single time

So detection is not the ceiling at all.

claim: GAP NOBODY IS WORKING: the public 0.938-family pipeline runs a motion-relink stage that rebuilds the edge list from a one-to-one Hungarian assignment BEFORE its safe-div step, which destroys every fork the upstream ILP produced. Any team that inherited that post-processing has made all upstream division work invisible - which explains a plateau of division_jaccard ~= 0 across ~400 teams.
quote: In the public 0.938 pipeline family the motion-relink stage rebuilds the edge list from a one-to-one Hungarian assignment before safe-div runs, so every fork the ILP produced is destroyed there. If you inherit that post-processing, any division work upstream of it is invisible.

claim: A distance gate alone CANNOT separate real sister pairs from broken continuations: calibrated sister separation is 7.24 um while the median interior-orphan jump is 8.5-10 um. Whatever decides daughter-vs-broken-track has to use appearance, parent motion history, or better detector localisation.
quote: Jose calibrated sister separation at 7.24 um from the real lineage edges; my orphan median is 8.5-10 um. A distance gate cannot separate the two populations.

claim: CONSENSUS IS WRONG about why divisions hurt. The strongest public evidence that divisions are dangerous is ISAKA Tsuyoshi's rule-based ablation where adding division edges moved LB 0.784 -> 0.778. Given that division FPs only count in annotated regions (~2.8%), that -0.006 is far too large to be a division-term loss; it is almost certainly an EDGE-term loss from the second arc creating edge FPs plus added nodes paying the node-count penalty.
quote: 3 + gap closing 0.807 0.784 v3 / 4 + division edges 0.810 0.778 v4 ... division edges hurt (0.784 → 0.778) and gap closing was roughly neutral.

claim: Detection, not linking, was the single biggest lever for the best public rule-based pipeline: multi-scale DoG with scale-space max took LB from 0.786 to 0.826 (+0.040) with no learning at all, reaching 7th/344 at the time.
quote: Detection was the biggest lever. Just taking DoG at multiple scales and using the scale-space max jumped LB from 0.786 → 0.826 (+0.040). In contrast, division edges hurt (0.784 → 0.778) and gap closing was roughly neutral.
